title: Repeat badge scan
prompt:
A door logs badge IDs in order; return true if the same ID appears twice with at most k scans between their positions (index distance <= k), else false.

- badges has 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^9 and 10^9.
- 0 <= k <= 100,000. Two scans at indices i < j count when badges[i] == badges[j] and j - i <= k.
- Return a boolean.
hints: Comparing every pair within distance k is O(n·k). For each scan, which earlier scan of the same ID matters most?
Only the most recent earlier occurrence of a value can be the closest one. Remember it in a hash map.
Walk left to right: if badges[j] is in the map and j - last[badges[j]] <= k, return true; otherwise store last[badges[j]] = j.

solution.explanation: For any value, the nearest earlier occurrence is the latest one seen, so a map from value to its last index is enough. Each scan checks that single candidate and then overwrites it, giving one pass with constant-time hash lookups.

complexity.notes: Expected O(1) per hash operation. A sliding set of the last k values gives O(min(n, k)) space instead.

followUps: Rewrite it with a set holding only the last k values so memory is O(min(n, k)).
